business_problem: Broadcasters needed a faster and more affordable way to create premium video at high volume, but traditional studio production and human-presenter workflows were too slow and expensive for always-on, frequently updated content channels.
solution_summary: Hour One built its Reals self-service video platform on NVIDIA GPUs with NVIDIA CUDA, NVIDIA cuDNN, and NVIDIA RTX so broadcasters can turn text into fully produced videos with virtual presenters in minutes. Users select a layout, choose from virtual characters or custom avatars, and submit script text through a browser-based cloud workflow. Under the hood, GPU-accelerated training pipelines build and refresh the models behind virtual humans, while the same cloud clusters handle inference and 3D rendering for finished scenes and virtual sets. The stack combines high-memory GPU compute for AI models with RTX-accelerated rendering so Hour One can serve generative video and avatar production from a single platform rather than separate media and ML systems. This architecture gives customers like RAN and DeFiance Media near-instant text-to-video generation and a practical way to publish premium broadcast content without the cost and limits of traditional studio workflows.

solution_components.name: Reals
solution_components.role: Provides the self-service web platform where broadcasters create videos from text with virtual presenters and sets.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA GPUs
solution_components.role: Deliver the cloud compute used for AI model training, inference, and media pipeline acceleration.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA CUDA
solution_components.role: Accelerates the model-training and media-processing workloads behind Hour One's virtual humans.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA cuDNN
solution_components.role: Speeds deep-learning training and inference for the state-of-the-art models used in the platform.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA RTX
solution_components.role: Supports 3D rendering for virtual sets, avatars, and broadcast-ready video output.

data_flow: Broadcasters enter text and choose layouts or avatars in Reals, Hour One's cloud pipelines train and run models on NVIDIA GPUs with CUDA and cuDNN, RTX-backed rendering produces the final virtual scenes, and finished videos are published to broadcast and digital channels.
business_outcome: Hour One helped broadcasters produce AI-generated video in minutes, launch new premium content series with near-instant turnaround, run a 24/7 virtual-anchor format more economically, and create highly monetizable video without the overhead of traditional studio production.
architecture_clues: Hour One serves its cloud offering through a browser-based workflow rather than requiring local rendering infrastructure.
The same GPU-backed cloud clusters handle both AI model workloads and 3D rendering.
Customers can start from a library of virtual humans or commission custom synthetic hosts.
evidence_quotes: With its self-service platform, Reals, broadcasters can access Hour One's technology more easily than ever, generating fully-produced videos automatically in just minutes.
The NVIDIA GPU, CUDA, and CudNN frameworks enable the team to train state-of-the-art models at a fast pace to meet customer needs.
Our cloud offering enables our customers to enjoy all the benefits of Generative AI and 3D rendering through their web browser with a few clicks.

Using NVIDIA's solutions, the team at Hour One was able to boost all their high-compute, high-memory-intensive workloads, including complex AI and media pipelines on the GPU and 3D rendering in their cloud clusters.
Near-instant AI video generation simply from text inputs is a highly cost-effective way to generate premium video that is highly monetizable.
